description: We are a creative team passionate about Earth science, space, digital media, and storytelling. We aim to transform Earth observation data into engaging audio and visual experiences by combining research, design, and innovation. We value teamwork, curiosity, and experimentation, and we are eager to explore new tools and technical skills to create an impactful and accessible solution for the Earth Information Jukebox challenge.
summary:
**Earth Pulse – Turning Earth's Data into Sound**

Earth science data is often presented through complex maps, charts, and visualizations, making it difficult for children and non-specialists to understand and limiting accessibility for blind and visually impaired individuals.

To address this challenge, our team, **AsterLink**, developed **Earth Pulse**, an interactive educational platform that transforms NASA Earth science data into meaningful piano sounds synchronized with visual changes.

Using NASA's nighttime lights visualizations from 2012 to 2023, based on VIIRS satellite observations, our prototype allows users to explore how Earth's nighttime illumination changes over time. Different data values are represented through corresponding musical notes, creating an engaging multisensory learning experience.

The platform also includes a children's mode with interactive educational games, accessibility options for visually impaired users, and Arabic and English language support.

Earth Pulse addresses NASA's **The Earth Information Jukebox** challenge by making scientific information easier to explore through both sound and sight. We believe understanding our planet should be accessible, engaging, and enjoyable for everyone.
details:
Earth Pulse – Project Details

How Our Project Works

Earth Pulse is an interactive, multisensory educational platform developed by Team AsterLink to make NASA Earth science data more accessible, understandable, and engaging.

Our prototype focuses on NASA's nighttime lights visualizations from 2012 to 2023, based on observations from the VIIRS satellite sensor.

Users can select a region, explore changes over time, and experience scientific information through synchronized visuals and piano sounds. The platform uses a data-to-sound mapping approach, where changes in numerical values are represented through changes in musical notes.

Instead of simply watching a visualization, users can interact with the information, explore different years, and discover patterns through both sight and sound.

Features and Benefits

  • Interactive Sonification: Transforms data variations into piano notes, creating an alternative way to explore scientific information.
  • Children's Mode: Introduces educational games and interactive questions to make learning more enjoyable.
  • Accessibility Mode (Under Development): We are developing a dedicated mode for blind and visually impaired users. This feature aims to provide audio-based navigation, spoken explanations, and an accessible way to explore scientific data independently. It is not yet fully implemented in our current prototype.
  • Bilingual Support: Provides Arabic and English options to reach a wider audience.
  • Interactive Exploration: Allows users to explore geographical regions and changes across different years.

Tools and Technologies

Our team used NASA's Scientific Visualization Studio (SVS) and VIIRS nighttime lights resources as scientific references.

We used Microsoft Excel to organize and analyze data, Manus AI to develop our interactive website prototype, ChatGPT to support concept development and educational content, and Canva to design our presentation.

Our development process relies on AI-assisted web development and existing digital tools, without requiring specialized hardware.

Creativity and Innovation

What makes Earth Pulse different is that sound is not simply background music. Our goal is to make scientific data itself the source of sound, allowing users to hear changes that are traditionally communicated through colors, maps, and charts.

By combining sonification, interactive storytelling, accessibility features, and educational games, we aim to transform complex scientific information into an enjoyable learning experience.

Intended Impact

Earth Pulse aims to make Earth science more inclusive, particularly for children, non-specialists, and people with visual impairments.

Our team considered scientific accuracy, accessibility, ease of use, educational value, and user engagement throughout the design process.

Our current prototype demonstrates the interactive experience. However, the dedicated accessibility mode remains under development, and further validation of the numerical data-to-sound mapping and accessibility testing are important next steps.

In the future, we hope to expand Earth Pulse to other NASA Earth datasets, enabling more people to explore climate, environmental changes, and other scientific phenomena through sound.

Our vision is simple: Earth science should not only be something we see, but something everyone can experience, understand, and enjoy.
